title: [RFC] Megatron FSDP v2 partial CUDA Graph capture and MoE composition validation
body:
## Motivation

Integrate Megatron FSDP v2 with Transformer Engine partial CUDA Graph capture, including end-to-end MoE composition validation. Selected compute runs in graphs while dynamic MoE operations and FSDP communication remain eager. Implementation: #9112. This addresses the [request to overlap non-captured and captured regions](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/9113#issuecomment-6761677082).

Graphs require stable compute-weight addresses, current parameter values, and correct FSDP gather/reduction ordering. Direct TE graph replay bypasses the module hooks that enforce that ordering; freeing gathered storage invalidates graph addresses. The design retains existing compute buffers and restores normal FSDP module entry around replay.

## Initial scope

| Dimension | Support |
|---|---|
| Precision and execution | BF16 without symmetric memory; fixed shapes and microbatch schedule |
| Capture regions | Attention, dense MLP, router, router-paired preprocess |
| Parallelism and sharding | TP=PP=CP=1; existing EP and gradient accumulation; ZeRO-1/2/3 |
| Validated compositions | GPT/Hybrid, attention/MLA, grouped/shared MoE experts |
| Eager regions | Dynamic dispatch/combine, routed experts, FSDP communication and optimizer |

Whole-layer capture, FP8/FP4, recomputation and TP/PP/CP expansion are outside this scope. The dedicated `overlap_moe_expert_parallel_comm` schedule is unsupported.

## Design

| Path | Execution |
|---|---|
| Eager | FSDP hooks gather/wait/prefetch around ordinary compute, then reduce completed gradients. Normal reshard/release applies. |
| Capture | Gather and retain compute buffers; suspend owned execution hooks and gradient-completion accounting during TE warmup/capture. Restore hooks and sharded bindings afterward; no optimizer step. |
| Replay | Enter the normal module boundary; hooks refresh/wait/prefetch around graph compute and prepare backward reductions. Reshard bindings while retaining graph-referenced storage. |

Four changes preserve these contracts:

1. **Capture isolation — [`fsdp_cuda_graph_capture()`](https://github.com/WEIXILIN0307/Megatron-LM/blob/26714de5265eb2ac593dc66f17f3f02062058359/megatron/core/distributed/fsdp/src/megatron_fsdp/experimental/module.py#L243).** Gather/retain weights on an idle unit and suspend only its execution hooks. Gradient callbacks skip training completion accounting during capture. `finally` restores hooks, capture state and sharded bindings.
2. **Module entry — [`_call_cuda_graph()`](https://github.com/WEIXILIN0307/Megatron-LM/blob/26714de5265eb2ac593dc66f17f3f02062058359/megatron/core/distributed/fsdp/src/megatron_fsdp/experimental/module.py#L282).** Temporarily use the graph callable as `forward`, invoke `nn.Module.__call__()`, then restore `forward`. This preserves forward hooks and the backward autograd boundary. Capture bypasses this entry while hooks are suspended.
3. **Stable storage, fresh contents — [`_retain_unsharded_storage`](https://github.com/WEIXILIN0307/Megatron-LM/blob/26714de5265eb2ac593dc66f17f3f02062058359/megatron/core/distributed/fsdp/src/megatron_fsdp/experimental/parameter_group.py#L476).** Retain gathered allocation across reshard, but invalidate readiness. The next unshard refreshes weights in the same buffer and records a new event; compute waits before reading it.
4. **Lifetime — [`create_cudagraphs()` / `delete_cuda_graphs()`](https://github.com/WEIXILIN0307/Megatron-LM/blob/26714de5265eb2ac593dc66f17f3f02062058359/megatron/core/transformer/cuda_graphs.py#L3031).** The helper owns capture/install/teardown and clones mutable RNG state for rollback. Tested MCore failures restore capture/RNG/training state and reset returned graphs before releasing retained storage. Deletion synchronizes GPU work and destroys graph references before freeing buffers; recapture uses a new helper with the existing model/optimizer.

**Stable address does not imply stale weights:** retention preserves allocation; unshard refreshes contents and readiness events order access. Gradient/optimizer sharding is unchanged.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    state "Idle: sharded bindings" as Idle
    state "Capture: gather, retain, suspend owned hooks" as Capture
    state "Graphs live: hooks restored, storage retained" as Live
    state "Invocation: refresh/wait, then replay" as Replay
    Idle --> Capture: create_cudagraphs
    Capture --> Live: success and restore sharded bindings
    Capture --> Idle: tested MCore failure resets graphs then releases storage
    Live --> Replay: normal module call
    Replay --> Live: reshard bindings and invalidate readiness
    Live --> Idle: reset graphs then release retention
```

## Communication dependencies

The existing compute, all-gather and reduction streams are reused. All-gather and reduction may share a stream under the existing runtime policy. The timeline below describes the ordering verified by the per-unit event records in Evidence.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Compute stream
    participant A as All-gather stream
    participant R as Reduction stream(s)
    C-->>A: Root wait_stream(C) after prior compute/optimizer work
    A->>A: Refresh/gather unit i then record E_AG_i
    A-->>C: Compute waits on E_AG_i
    par Successor prefetch
        A->>A: Gather unit i+1
    and Current compute
        C->>C: Replay graph for unit i
    end
    Note over C,A: Reshard orders storage reuse after compute
    R-->>C: Wait for prior reduction/staging-buffer reuse
    C->>C: Pack completed gradients
    C-->>R: Reduction waits for the pack
    par Ready communication
        R->>R: Reduce-scatter and accumulate
    and Independent later compute
        C->>C: Replay a later backward graph
    end
    R-->>C: finish_grad_sync joins submitted reductions
    C->>C: Consume gradients then update shards
```

`unshard()` inserts the current unit's compute wait before submitting successor prefetch, so compute need not wait for the successor's gather. Gradient packing waits for staging-buffer reuse; reduction then waits for the pack. `finish_grad_sync()` joins reductions before gradient consumption. These are stream dependencies, allowing independent AG/RS and graph compute to overlap without per-unit device-wide synchronization.

Here `i+1` is a successor in the FSDP execution order, which can be the expert unit in the same TransformerLayer. Same-unit weight/gradient dependencies and same-microbatch routing → dispatch → expert → combine dependencies remain. This integration enables FSDP/graph concurrency; it does not implement EP dispatch/combine overlap.

## Tradeoffs and memory cost

| Approach | Decision |
|---|---|
| Retain existing buffers; replay through module hooks | Chosen: reuse FSDP ownership and communication. The cost follows existing unit boundaries, including eager weights in the same unit. |
| Capture communication inside graphs | Expands capture scope and requires additional collective-order and dependency validation. |
| Separate graph-weight buffers | Adds storage, refresh copies and binding/lifetime rules that existing compute buffers avoid. |
| Smaller FSDP units | May reduce residency, but changes parameter ownership and collective granularity. Consider only if measured cost warrants it. |

Per-unit retained residency is the sum of non-alias gathered-buffer storage: approximately `2 × owned_parameter_elements` bytes for BF16, including padding. Replicated aliases add none. Cost follows existing FSDP ownership, including eager weights owned by a captured unit.

The proxy retains **32.074 MiB × 16 units = 513.188 MiB/rank**. Peak memory also includes activations, graph pools, communication and caches; capture/replay can OOM when eager fits.

## Evidence

### Correctness

The [tested composition](https://github.com/WEIXILIN0307/Megatron-LM/commit/a8a842466016426769ca479eac22a6354e4668a4) includes prerequisites #9372/#9374. All [28 representative cases](https://github.com/WEIXILIN0307/Megatron-LM/tree/4c50d26554c39dcdab59e4bc6552b9f643a8557a/mfsdp-v2-core-split-20261112/reduced-tests-20261112) pass per rank on two PRO GPUs: model/scopes, sharding, numerical/optimizer parity, evaluation, RNG, lifecycle and failure recovery. [Four-GPU tests](https://github.com/WEIXILIN0307/Megatron-LM/tree/c9d6469a76afdcf36e5428cc826cae4b708af15b/mfsdp-v2-core-split-20261112) also cover EP2/expert-DP2.

New real-text experiments use stock `pretrain_gpt.py`, WikiText-103 and a **2.09B GPT MoE proxy**: 16 layers, hidden 2048, 16 experts, top-8, BF16/ZeRO-3, sequence 1024, microbatch 1, GA2, dropout 0.1. Capture selects `attn moe_router moe_preprocess`. All 45 per-rank losses match exactly across eager/graph repeats within each topology, with no skipped steps. Separate EP2 runs compare complete logical local-shard snapshots at steps 4/12: parameters, main weights and Adam state are byte-identical. Gradients are numerically identical; one expert gradient has 4756 signed-zero differences (`−0.0` versus `+0.0`), with maximum absolute difference 0 and matching zero-normalized hashes.

### Concurrency and event dependencies

![Recorded FSDP/graph kernels and matched readiness events](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WEIXILIN0307/Megatron-LM/c8883d7b176494c59a7f32ef585f655471bcff11/mfsdp-v2-core-split-20261112/gap-closure-20261113/fsdp-unit-event-timeline.png)

The four-A6000 EP2/expert-DP2 recording matches **132 readiness producer/wait chains/rank**, linking **all 64 graph launches to their own readiness waits**. Actual target units/groups and DeviceMesh dimensions identify communication ownership. Each rank records 32 successor-prefetch/graph intersections and 298 reduction packing/finish event pairs. The figure traces layer 0 graph launch 3505 and expert prefetch AG 3390 to their distinct dependencies, including event 23709/generation 31 from stream 36 to compute stream 16.

Expert-DP AG/RS overlap graph compute; ordinary-DP AG/RS and EP token A2A do not in this trace. Event-completion tracing is disabled. One GPU is shared, so kernel intersections establish concurrency, not performance; host API durations are not device wait times.

EP2 preprocess graphs contain routing-count gathers: 16 captured operators, each with 16 int64 elements on the EP group, replayed twice under GA2. Capture records **zero FSDP parameter gathers**; count metadata is distinguished from FSDP weight AG and token A2A.

### Performance, memory and communication hiding

Each mode has three 45-step runs on idle A6000s with identical model/data/software, timing steps 16–45 without profiling or hashing. Time averages the slowest rank's window; memory is the maximum per-rank PyTorch steady peak across repeats, excluding external CUDA/NCCL allocations.

| Topology | Eager → graph, ms/step | Step-time change | Eager → graph peak allocated / reserved |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 2 GPUs, EP2/expert-DP1, global batch 4 | 1178.77 → 1024.31 | **13.10% lower**; throughput +15.08% | 21.720 / 23.814 → 20.495 / 25.391 GiB |
| 3 GPUs, EP1/expert-DP3, global batch 6 | 2584.68 → 2598.32 | **0.53% higher** | 16.354 / 17.801 → 15.124 / 19.402 GiB |

Max-rank capture-helper setup spans 2.325–2.916 s for EP2 and 2.103–2.349 s for EP1. Retained weights are 513.188 MiB/rank; this does not explain the entire allocator/pool delta. The earlier graph OOM under a 17.360 GiB allocator budget remains a capacity limitation. The new runs establish successful matched comparisons with adequate headroom.

An EP1 measurement control serializes graph replay against FSDP streams, preserving numerical work, buffers and scope. Three runs average **2733.70 ms/step**, versus **2598.32 ms** normally: **135.38 ms/step (4.95%) less time**. Serialization eliminates trace intersections. A single same-count empty-stream placebo retains intersections and takes **2586.51 ms/step**, with comparable CPU enqueue cost (~3 ms/step). All losses match. This supports an end-to-end scheduling benefit, not an exact hidden-network-time measurement; EP1 graph remains slightly slower than eager.

### Failure boundaries and limitations

Stock TE 2.20.2 can retain temporary hooks after a warmup exception. [NVIDIA/TransformerEngine#3862](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/3862) adds independent cleanup and a failure/retry regression; isolated overlays pass focused TE checks and two-rank GPT/Hybrid MoE retry/state-parity checks. Normal-path MCore correctness, timing and trace evidence above uses unmodified TE 2.20.2. Arbitrary TE exceptions and fatal CUDA/NCCL errors remain outside the recovery guarantee; full upstream CI is pending.

The evidence qualifies the stated proxy/configurations. It does not qualify EP dispatch/combine overlap, full OLMoE, long-run convergence or general scaling. [Reproduction bundle](https://github.com/WEIXILIN0307/Megatron-LM/tree/c8883d7b176494c59a7f32ef585f655471bcff11/mfsdp-v2-core-split-20261112/gap-closure-20261113) contains exact commands, software/data hashes, per-rank reports, sanitized trace inputs, event analysis and detailed logs.

## Delivery and review

#9372 (evaluation cursor) and #9374 (native DTensor loading) are independent prerequisites. #9112 owns the capture/replay integration and MoE validation; [NVIDIA/TransformerEngine#3862](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/3862) independently owns warmup-exception cleanup.
